sections.title: Robust sequential tests and endpoint qualifications

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-robust-hypothesis-testing-C005 (partial): The declared proof (proved=annex:p15.huber.tv.pair) is incomplete for the k_+ half of the claim 'There are unique k_-,k_+ in [0,1] satisfying ...'. Annex lines 145-146 handle existence and uniqueness of k_+ only by saying the decreasing upper-transfer function int(p_1-ks)_+ dmu 'has the analogous property'. That is a 'similarly' deferral: the property itself (1 at k=0, 0 at k=1, continuous, strictly decreasing wherever positive) is neither stated nor proved. A second, smaller gap: the argument for ell=max{c',min(c'',r)}=q_1/q_0 (annex 165-169) works out the ratio on each region but never derives that the transfer regions {k_-s>p_1} and {p_1>k_+s} are exactly {r<c'} and {r>c''}. It only asserts that they match the source's eq. (6).

ED26-P15-CH-robust-hypothesis-testing-C008 (partial): Item 3 claims 'Such a choice exists, including the possible zero-risk singular case', and the declared proof does not prove this with written steps. Annex lines 313-321 restate a general bracketing fact for quantiles and support it only with 'This follows directly from the inverse-CDF construction in the preceding proof, or from the same continuity argument as thm:p15-likelihood-threshold'. That is a pointer standing in for the derivation. The cited lemma is stated and proved for P_0 with a likelihood ratio that is finite P_0-almost surely, not for the mixture M=L_0Q_0^n+L_1Q_1^n, under which T_n can carry an infinite atom. No threshold c with M(T_n>c)<=L_1<=M(T_n>=c) is derived, and neither is the randomization that fills the difference. Items 1 and 2, the item-3 minimax comparison and the zero-radius case are written in full.

ED26-P15-CH-robust-sequential-endpoints-C012 (partial): The failure condition 'unstated assumption' holds: the entry never states its observation space. The exact identity sup_{R in H_1} E_R N_{a,b} = E_{Q_1}N_{a,b} = (1-(3/5)^r)/(2/5), and its annex derivation at lines 487-514 ('mass p at one ranges over [2/5,3/5]'; worst case at p=2/5), hold only if every contamination is supported on {0,1}. The chapter's own setting allows an arbitrary measurable space and any contamination H (def lines 14-18). Under the convention r=1 on the common null set (robust-hypothesis-testing.tex 81-84), with densities taken as zero off {0,1}, every point outside {0,1} gets score 4/5. Example: on X={0,1,2} with H=delta_2 and a=3c, E_R N is about 2.168, which exceeds E_{Q_1}N=49/25. So the stated supremum holds only under the unstated restriction X={0,1}. The other assertions in the entry are written.

sections.title: Repeated fixed-sample tests and optional-stopping failures

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-METHOD-sequential-evidence-C03 (partial): The success condition needs each claimed stopping/error guarantee to be shown, by written steps, to hold for the actual stopping procedure. Five guarantees have one case discharged by 'similarly' or 'the same argument' instead. (1) thm:p15-se-deadline: the P_1 bound P_1(T<=N) >= P_1(Z_N>=a) is given 'by the same argument' (handbook/annex/p15/sequential-evidence.tex 418-419). (2) thm:p15-se-lattice: the upper terminal support a_0..a_0+g_2-1, which the exact exit probabilities and gamma depend on, 'follows similarly' (annex 195-196). (3) thm:p15-se-truncation: the alternative-error bound beta_N <= beta' + P_1(b<Z_N<=0) is a one-sentence pointer; the coupling and union-bound steps are written only for the null half (annex 437-439), although the held Wald 1945 source writes both halves at (4.63)-(4.66), printed p.153. (4) thm:p15-se-binomial: the eta constant used in the operating-characteristic bounds is obtained 'similarly' (annex 260-261). (5) thm:p15-se-transform: the r<0 integrability case is handled 'in the same calculation' (annex 343-344). Under the audit rule these proofs are partial. Every other stopping/error proof on the route is written in full: termination, coupled error inequalities, the dependent-density version, nominal boundaries, operating-characteristic bounds, the absorption recursion, repeated independent looks, and all results of the w02b-p15-061 chapter.
